notes.title: Devlog #28: Growing vegetables on Mars
notes.content:
Dear Martians! 

While waiting for the prologue version, here’s a new devlog for you! ːsteamhappyː

Today we would like to talk about vegetable cultivation inside your Mars Base, which will be a crucial part of your mission. As a colonist, one of your main tasks will be to establish a reliable food source on Mars. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31460179/cc203c649c9d8e211d0b0d5d551bb97aed220a46.png

Inside the Main HQ, you can grow potatoes and beetroots, but before you start cultivating plants, you need to build devices, which will allow you to do it, e.g. hydroponic shelves and optionally plant incubator. At your disposal you’ll have a seed tool used for planting seeds. Besides, you have to make sure that your base has power and water connection because your plants need light and water.🌱

https://i.imgur.com/6kftIqC.gif

The next important step is planting seeds, but you have to choose if you want to plant seeds directly on hydroponic shelves or plant them in plant incubator first, which will speed up germination. The choice is yours! 

https://i.imgur.com/Mis4Ivt.gif

If you would like to plant seeds in an incubator first, remember that once the crops have germinated, you have to replant them into hydroponic shelves. Growing potatoes and beetroots on hydroponic trays from the beginning won’t require replanting them later but it will take longer. In the full game there will also be additional steps where you can replant your crops into fields and greenhouses.

While cultivating, you have to monitor the parameters (like: temperature and water level) on an ongoing basis and manage resources wisely if you want to grow food successfully. 🥔

https://i.imgur.com/HcXOZNO.gif

The prologue is close to launch. Stay tuned for upcoming updates. If you have any questions or just want to talk with devs and other future colonists, feel free to join our Discord server!

Best Regards,
Occupy Mars Team

https://store.steampowered.com/app/758690/Occupy_Mars_The_Game/

notes.title: The Steam Game Festival Summary
notes.content:
Dear Martians! 

It's time to summarize The Steam Game Festival! 

First of all, we would like to thank you for playing Occupy Mars Demo during the summer festival! We've gathered tons of valuable feedback and suggestions that we couldn't have collected in any other way.

notes.title: Devlog #27: Water Extraction on Mars
notes.content:
Dear Martians!

While waiting for the beta - here's another interesting DevLog for you. ːsteamhappyː

Last time we told you about generating power on Mars, and today we would like to bring up another important topic, which is providing access to water. Since you want to succeed in colonizing Mars, you have to know the basics of establishing a self-sustaining colony. 

https://i.imgur.com/jhVJcj5.png

Water is essential for life and your whole Colony simply needs access to it. As a colonist, one of your main tasks will be to establish a water supply system. But how to get water on Mars? First, you have to build wells to extract water from Martian soil. The “wells” in our game are not typical pumps, instead they are futuristic extractors which can heat the soil below and extract the water from the molecules in the ground. 

https://i.imgur.com/7yW72pl.png

The wells can be built near water rich spots, which can be found by using a spectral detector. Extracted water will be stored in the water tanks. Wells also have their own tanks, so you can distribute the water directly from a well to a building. 

https://i.imgur.com/Izndbm8.gif

To maximize the efficiency of water extraction you can always use a pump station to have complete control over your water distribution. For example, you can control the amount of water supplied to each of the buildings with the use of a special panel. But first, you have to connect the pump station to your base and other buildings.

https://i.imgur.com/wCYey0G.png

Stay tuned for upcoming updates. If you have any questions or just want to know more about the game, feel free to join our Discord server! 

Best Regards, 
Occupy Mars Team

notes.title: Devlog #26: Generating power on Mars
notes.content:
Dear Martians!

Today we are back with the new interesting content from the game for you!

Self-sustaining Martian Colony requires constant source of energy. Once you’ve built your first base you have to provide energy access to power your buildings and other facilities. 

https://i.imgur.com/Gq7E7vs.gif

Electricity is needed to power the equipment and heating system inside the buildings. Of course you also need electricity to have a light inside your buildings. Take greenhouse, for example. In order to grow plants you have to provide light, which is the key element of photosynthesis. 

What is more, sustaining life requires you to constantly pump out carbon dioxide that easily accumulates in hermetically closed quarters. Electrical power is everything when it comes to survival on Mars. 

https://i.imgur.com/bhWUvaq.gif

Electricity can be generated from solar panels. For energy storage you have to build batteries. During the Martian nights, batteries provide electrical power and keep the whole Colony supplied with electricity. The batteries recharge during the day so the whole process can repeat until you come up with a different method of producing electricity. Solar panels and batteries can be upgraded. 

https://i.imgur.com/9Wq2MH9.gif

For energy management you have to build transformers that have to be connected to the batteries and the buildings by cables. Once everything is connected properly, all of your buildings in the colony are supplied with electricity. When your colony eventually grows bigger, you’ll need more effective power supplies, but this is the topic for another devlog. 

https://i.imgur.com/myvlUnz.gif

If you have any questions or just want to know more about the game, feel free to join our Discord server! 

Best Regards,
Occupy Mars Team

https://store.steampowered.com/app/758690/Occupy_Mars_The_Game/

notes.title: Devlog #25: Construction: Design Mode
notes.content:
Dear Martians! 

It’s 2020 and you’re soon going to Mars! Good preparation is the key to the success of the mission, so today we’re continuing our devlog series with another important topic. 

In previous devlogs we showed that establishing a self-sustaining Martian Colony plays a crucial role in colonizing Mars. But building a Martian Habitat is a difficult task due to uneven terrain of the planet. There are also some places where you can’t build anything so choosing a good building site is essential.

https://i.imgur.com/Bq3VDrP.gif

Today’s post focuses on the building process in Occupy Mars and is complementary to Devlog #17. After you've gathered resources and printed enough Building Materials - constructing actual buildings begins with the design mode. First, you have to select a building from the building menu and check if it can be placed in selected location. Remember that you can only place it there if the outline appears in green colour.            When the building turns red, it means that you can’t build it there.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31460179/6505f954c89b3346f2e15b709d152cfcd51ac107.png

You can freely try different locations for the building. At this stage, you can adjust the foundation height of the building, which enables you to build on uneven terrain, but once you actually place it on the soil, its colour turns to white and you can no longer move it around the map. If you don’t like the outlined construction that you've already placed, you can still destroy it without losing resources by using a grinder.

https://i.imgur.com/3RwRVA1.gif

You can connect different building sections or corridors by snapping them one by one or (in case of uneven terrain) by joining them with one of the types of the “slope corridor” - which is especially helpful when you want to connect constructions built on different levels. 

Remember that if the foundations of your building are not high enough, you will have problems with adjusting other structures or objects. If the construction has high foundations, you’ll have to build ramps in order to get inside. Keep in mind that ramps can only be attached to airlocks. When it comes to airlocks - remember to build them in pairs, otherwise the inside pressure can push you away when opening the door.

Of course, placing an “outline” of your base is just the beginning, now you need to “get your hands dirty” and make use of your Crusher, 3D Printer, Blowtorch & Heavy Rover, and actually build the designed base. 

https://i.imgur.com/yQ3MDG9.gif

In 2020, you’re going to colonise the Red Planet, and some of you are also going to become engineers there. Let’s occupy Mars and fix Mars Rovers! 

If you have any questions or just want to know more about the game, feel free to join our Discord server!

Best Regards,
Occupy Mars Team

notes.title: An Opportunity for Merry Xmas!
notes.content:
Dear Martians!

When NASA announced that the Opportunity Rover mission officially ended on 13th Feb 2019, we were all very sad. This "little rover that could" along with his twin brother Spirit landed on Mars in January 2004.

Since that time he gave us amazing science and pictures. He was designed to operate for 90 days, but he worked tirelessly for 15 years! 🖤

We thought it's not fair that the Rover is to stay broken on Mars forever, so we decided that if there's anything we could do to bring him (and other Mars Rovers) back to life we would do it! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31460179/df188394b25bdf22590a8683b7d80ee5fe765b26.png

We decided to create a smaller Spin-off game in the "Occupy Mars" Universe, where you play as an engineer intending to fix Oppy, and other historic Rovers that ever explored the Red Planet. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31460179/907e5e20bc3800048a7295d42b3d2866ddad1609.png

As you know, Occupy Mars is an open world, sandbox, hard science-fiction game about Mars colonization. The goal here is to survive, build and maintain a growing martian colony. You wouldn't have time for fixing Mars Rovers.  

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31460179/b23db859bdebf30c10bc80d694279e01ee24c13d.png

Making a "Mechanic" game is an experiment for us. We also noticed that people who play "Mechanic" series games are usually not interested in sandbox or survival games. Thanks to a Spin-Off game, we hope to interest more people in Mars exploration and science.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/864680/Rover_Mechanic_Simulator

Rover Mechanic Simulator will be released in Steam Early Access on February 6th! 

We hope you will like this game as much as Occupy Mars. We would like to wish you a Merry Christmas and a Happy New Year 2020, where many of our games are going to come out! :) 
[previewyoutube=6UJMuR-ezXs;full][/previewyoutube] 
We've also prepared something special for you, so check out our Facebook Page! 
Feel free to join our Discord server! 

Best Regards,

notes.title: Devlog #24: Sleep Well and Occupy Mars
notes.content:
Dear Martians! 

How to succeed in colonizing Mars? The answer is getting enough sleep! 

Building a prosperous Martian colony requires lots of energy. When you are tired, you need to go to sleep. It will increase your stamina to the maximum level, so you’ll be strong enough to overcome any difficulties and occupy Mars. 

Red Planet has no mercy for people who don't take care of themselves. Good colonists know why sleep is so crucial. Apart from avoiding sleep deprivation and general tiredness, keeping regular bedtime is a great way to get through the Martian nights, when temperatures are critically low.

https://i.imgur.com/Tw4PGs3.png

Of course, you need a bed to get proper rest. Beds can be built in a hab and living capsules. But what if you are on an exploration trip, far away from your base? Don't worry, your Heavy Rover also has a fully functioning bed! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31460179/38f47dc8a3bffbbb798cdb8dbe3eae8777dfbcc3.png

notes.content:
https://i.imgur.com/fhtARef.gif

Dear Martians!

Creating a prosperous colony on Mars and surviving there requires lots of energy. You will have to take good care of yourself and make sure you don’t forget to eat nutritious food, which will give you strength to succeed in this mission! 

https://i.imgur.com/zB5ZyxV.gif

As you might know from previous devlogs, inside your greenhouse and main HQ, you will grow various crops in order to establish a reliable food source on Mars. When your crops are ripe, you will need to harvest them as soon as possible to prevent them from rotting. Your veggies and other agricultural products will be stored in the player’s inventory. They will all be ready for immediate consumption, but if you want to eat something more nutritious, you will have to prepare your food using a food processing unit.

https://i.imgur.com/MqUEfSf.gif

To make a meal, you can use one product or combine different products. You don’t have to follow specific recipes. When food processing is over, you can collect your meal from the machine’s tray and it will be automatically placed in your inventory.

notes.content:

Dear Martians! 

Main Hab (HQ) / Workshop is the most important construction in the Martian colony and a command centre of the base. It is a two storey building that consists of modules. It provides everything that’s needed to survive on Mars for a short time for one person. The Hab protects the player against radiation as well as the harsh environment of the planet and provides space and equipment for growing minimum amounts of food. 

Main Hab will be a cosy place for regaining the strength and a shelter with perfect view. Inside you will have a bed, so you can take a nap or go to sleep whenever you need. In the Main Workshop you’ll also have some space for Workbench and ChemLab to fix anything you need. Inside you will also have a 3D printer (necessary for printing spare parts) and a CO2 Scrubber which will help you maintain a breathable atmosphere.

Inside you can also create a small greenhouse and cultivate plants on hydroponic shelves. You will have specialistic devices, such as seed modification machine, plant incubator and food processing unit, but you won’t be able to fit everything in one Hab, so either choose wisely or prepare to expand your base.

notes.title: Devlog #17: Building Martian Base
notes.content:
https://i.imgur.com/aDtGhn0.gif

Dear Martians!

Building and upgrading the first base plays an important role in colonizing Mars, so today’s post is focused on this topic. 

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31460179/a6a7ed7278773f3017fc3bad4c46267c2ee1693f.png

Building constructions begins with “the design mode”. This stage is unlimited and won’t require using resources. First you have to place the “ghosts” of buildings anywhere you want and see if you’re satisfied with the results. You can freely change the ghost placement or destroy them by using a grinder, without losing resources. 

https://i.imgur.com/rxOmJv6.gif

You can place the building sections side by side to connect them or place it independently without any connection. If the modules are joined together, the pressure inside a buildings is compensated. When the constructions are set independently, you have to build two airlocks. Remember that designing, as well as building can be done on a flat terrain. 

https://i.imgur.com/yQ3MDG9.gif

When you already designed the constructions, you can start to build them with a welder tool. This process requires resources. Constructions can be built from modules and components which are printed by using a 3D printer. If you don’t have enough materials, you won’t be able to produce required components. You can destroy buildings using a grinder tool, but it is connected with a partial loss of materials.  

https://i.imgur.com/h25c1FU.gif

As you progress through the game you will be able to build and upgrade another base - your dreamed martian base! In that case you'll need lots of resources to produce required components. Future devlog will give you the details of the 3D printer, which is an essential device in construction process.

notes.title: Devlog #15: The Workbench
notes.content:
https://i.imgur.com/gIHwJsU.png

Dear Martians!

The Workbench will allow you to repair broken parts of the Printed Circuit Boards that are used in the electronic equipment available in the game. It is equipped with soldering station with hot air tool and soldering iron. On the workbench you can also find multimeter station and a case with the new components for the PCBs. 

As part of the Workbench you will have access to a helping multi-display, which will allow you to zoom and diagnose even the tiniest SMD components.

https://i.imgur.com/F5hShAz.gif

First step in PCB repair will be desoldering. In order to disassemble the damaged components, you have to melt the solder alloy by using a hot air tool. 

https://i.imgur.com/aG5pFfA.gif

Then you can replace a faulty compoment with a new element. 

https://i.imgur.com/XIinqQy.gif

Next you can use the soldering iron to solder the new component back into the board. 

Sometimes a PCB will also have broken conductive tracks. They can be fixed by using the soldering station as well. Place the soldering iron on the broken track and put new solder along it’s path. 

https://i.imgur.com/4emkn9z.gif

Once the process is done, you can use the multimeter station to check if the connections are fixed and the PCB is repaired. 

---

notes.content:

Dear Martians! 

Mars is a cold planet and the average temperature is much lower than on Earth. Due to the thin atmosphere of the Red Planet, the significant temperature drop can be observed. 

As we mentioned in previous devlog, fortunately the player has a weather forecast system which warns about the expected temperature drop and incoming natural events. The weather alerts will be received about an hour before the expected temperature drop or incoming weather phenomenon, so you will have enough time to take shelter inside a base or a heavy rover. 
When the atmospheric temperature is already very low or when the natural event strikes, the warning will appear on the screen. 

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31460179/5afe4c8f19606174e6514aa0eee971fc25690068.png

notes.content:
https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31460179/0c5135d8ee898337cb39c6fef5b79ad643e0619e.png

Dear Martians!

Solar storm is an another natural phenomenon that frequently occurs on the Red Planet. These events are often caused by the sudden and powerful solar flares, which are usually accompanied by a coronal mass ejection - a massive burst of solar wind. 

Solar storm increases radiation levels on the surface of the planet. During solar events, UV and X-rays are also released which could interfere with long-distance radio communication radars and devices that use these frequencies. 

Energetic particles emitted by the Sun are a big radiation hazard to people, because they can pass through the space suit, so it is important to take shelter inside a base or a Rover immediately! Fortunately the player has a weather forecast system which usually warns him about the incoming events.

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31460179/530283edfca768e9c0f60d247a47016763a2ed38.png

Solar storms could trigger Auroras at Mars, which can cover the entire planet, because the Red Planet has no strong magnetic field to concentrate the aurora near polar regions. 

https://i.imgur.com/ciWdX0R.gif

notes.title: Devlog #12: The Weather: part 1/3
notes.content:
https://i.imgur.com/bw0atQy.gif

Dear Martians!

Various atmospheric and astronomical phenomenons, such as meteor storms, sandstorms, solar storms often occur on Mars. Some of them could be extremely dangerous not only for the people, but also for buildings and equipment. In today’s post, you can learn about sandstorm and meteor shower. 


Meteor shower - astronomical phenomenon, very common on Mars, in which a number of meteors are observed to fall from one point in the sky carving fresh craters into the Martian surface. It occurs more than 200 times per year! usually when the orbit of the Red Planet goes through a meteor stream from the Asteroid Belt or through a tail of small comet fragments. 

During meteor storm it’s better to take shelter inside a base or a Rover, because you can get hit by a meteorite or by some debris from nearby devices. This phenomenon also causes damage to the infrastructure. It is important to remember about safety and don’t get too close to the damaged solar batteries or transformers - you can die from being electrocuted!


Sandstorm - atmospheric event that is formed when solar heating warms the Martian atmosphere and causes the air to move and lift large amounts of sand and dust. In reality they can last for months, covering even the entire planet, but in the game Mars won’t be that harsh. 

Sandstorms in the game will last hours, not months and cover only some part of the planet. Sand particles can cause damage to the equipment, vehicles and buildings. Remember to clean your equipment after the storm and fix your base as soon as possible! 

https://i.imgur.com/Gtk0Owl.gif

In the next devlog, you will read about other natural phenomenons that occur on the Red Planet.

notes.title: Devlog #4: Greenhouse
notes.content:
Dear Martians! 

One of the most important and also challenging task, will be to establish reliable food source on Mars. In order to achieve this, you will need to grow crops, because plants are the major source of food and oxygen on the Red Planet. You will have to build martian greenhouses for growing various plants. 

https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31460179/598482e75be4a6321e1c6e44f625c80bc83d40bd.png

Greenhouse

Greenhouse is a large building intended for cultivating plants in controlled environment. It provides required conditions for plant growth, such as: temperature, lighting and irrigation. You can control conditions in the greenhouse using a terminal. Moreover, it can also be used for air revitalization, water recycling, waste recycling and food processing. 

In the greenhouse you can use two methods of growing plants, such as: hydroponics (without soil, in hydroponic pot / container filled with water rich in minerals and nutrients) and traditional method - direct to soil. Plants growing in hydroponic pots or containers, have different needs than plants growing in the soil. You can generate the soil from organic material using the composter. 
The greenhouse also has a folding shield which helps you protect your crops during solar storms.

Plants cultivation

First, start seeds in a small hydroponic pots, which you can find on the side of the greenhouse. When seedlings grow taller, you can plant them directly to the soil, and then to the large containers. Plants need light (for the photosynthesis), carbon dioxide, water and nitrogen. Ideal soil should be rich in Nitrogen, which is a natural fertilizer that help plants grow healthy. If soil doesn’t contain enough nitrogen - plants will grow really slow and weak. 

Greenhouse is filled with the equipment which will help you with the cultivating, such as: 

 seed planting tool; 
 containers and pots; 
 hydroponic farm; 
 plant incubator;
 seed modification device;
 organic composter;
 terminals for controlling the conditions of a greenhouse.


Remember that your plants are quite fragile, you can’t allow the greenhouse to lose pressure, otherwise your food supplies may quickly disappear.

https://i.imgur.com/FWTNn8t.gif

One greenhouse should be enough for a few colonizers, but you will need to build more of them if you want to grow your colony. Later you will also be able to build garden domes, but that’s a story for another time ;) 

If you have any suggestions or topics, which you would like you to read about, feel free to let us know on our discord channel. Keep following us on social media! 

See you next week! ːsteamhappyː
Best Regards, 
Occupy Mars Team
